## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Isabelle Robinet's notice in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004, 2:401–65, DZ 714) gives the authoritative modern framing.

**Abstract**

The commentary is one of the **most influential Northern-Sòng readings of the *Dàodé jīng***. Its synthesis of scholarly-philological method with devotional Daoism was foundational for subsequent Sòng-Yuán Daoist commentarial tradition, and Chén Jǐngyuán was regarded as the **teacher-lineage** for [彭耜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E8%80%9C) Péng Sì (DZ 707 preface), [杜道堅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%81%93%E5%A0%85) Dù Dàojiān, [李道純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%81%93%E7%B4%94) Lǐ Dàochún, and many other later Daoist commentators.

The **1072 presentation** places the commentary at the height of the Wáng Ānshí 王安石 *xīn fǎ* 新法 reform era — in the same year that Wáng Ānshí's son [王雱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%9B%B1) Wáng Pōu composed his rival *Lǎozǐ* commentary. The two 1072 commentaries (Chén Jǐngyuán's Daoist and Wáng Pōu's Confucian-reformist) together define the late-Northern-Sòng imperial-court engagement with the *Dàodé jīng*.
